Relying instead on the prior review pass's specific, methodologically-described finding (verbatim duplicate confirmed by diff after stripping indentation, six tests, lines 136-303) plus corroboration that the current external test file exhibits exactly the rigor that finding attributed to it (ac_3 asserts exact fragment text at every position plus every adjacent-pair overlap substring; ac_6 performs full-string reconstruction with accents/nyet/emoji). No assertion gap found; treated as closed, not re-opened absent contrary evidence.

New, minor finding from this pass (not previously raised, not blocking): a handful of inline (non-doc) comments inside fragmentar()'s body narrate WHAT the next line does rather than WHY, e.g. 'Construir el fragmento como String a partir del rango de caracteres.' and 'Si hemos alcanzado el final, salir del bucle.' -- both restate the following statement in prose. This is a mild stylistic mismatch against presupuesto.rs's precedent voice (that function has zero inline body comments, relying entirely on its doc comment for WHY) and against 00-spec.yaml's didactic 'why, not what' invariant. Most of the other inline comments in the same function (validating first to avoid infinite loops/disproportionate allocation, advancing inicio to preserve overlap) do lean WHY-first, so this is a partial, low-severity gap, not a systemic failure -- noted, not made a fix_task, since it carries no functional risk and the required /// doc comments (the actual 'cross-module contract' per 01-blueprint.yaml) are genuinely WHY-first and complete.

Signature, error-before-touching-text ordering, size==0 rejection via the same >= check, no-ordinal-assignment, Vec<char> UTF-8 safety, empty-input handling, and no special-cased last-chunk branch were all re-checked directly against the current fragmentacion.rs and hold as specified.
